meta.title: Siaya County: ten-year fiscal history
meta.unit: KSh billion unless stated; revenue and pending bills in KSh million
meta.basis: Nominal (money of the day). Fiscal year runs 1 July to 30 June.
meta.note: Each year is read from the Controller of Budget annual county report for that year. Where two reports give different values for the same year, both are kept in 'alternates'.
gaps: FY2013/14: approved budget and pending bills not shown (only spending, absorption and revenue quoted in the FY2014/15 report). FY2014/15: pending recurrent bills were not reported.

FY2019/20: the Controller of Budget annual county report for this year is not in the Parliament library and cob.go.ke was unreachable (21 Nov 2026), so its approved budget and recurrent/development split, spending, absorption, own-source revenue target and pending bills are missing. Own-source revenue (KSh 179.43m) comes from the FY2020/21 report. The Senate report on that CoB report names Siaya only without figures. Figures from the county's own Budget Review and Outlook Paper and other documents are listed under supplementary and are not used in the series.
Audit opinions for FY2016/17 to FY2018/19 are missing for the reasons given under audits.

FY2025/26: only in-year reports (first quarter and first half) were found; they are kept under in_year and are not a full year. The annual FY2025/26 report's Part 2, which holds Siaya, is not in the Parliament library.

audits.label: Auditor-General opinion on the County Executive of Siaya's accounts
audits.note: Opinions for FY2014/15 and FY2015/16 come from a Senate committee compilation of Auditor-General opinions (annexes to the Senate fiduciary risk report, November 2018), not from the audit reports themselves, so they are graded lower; the FY2014/15 opinion may cover the County Executive and County Assembly together. Opinions for FY2016/17 to FY2018/19 are not shown: the Parliament library holds no County Executive of Siaya audit report for those years and the Auditor-General's site was unreachable when we tried. A civil-society summary gives an opinion for FY2016/17, but it is not a primary document, so it is not shown. FY2019/20 comes from a Senate committee report that quotes the audit, so it is graded lower. The first entry covers 16 months, not a full fiscal year, and the whole county government (executive and assembly together); the later entries cover the County Executive only.

pending_rollforward.label: Pending bills roll-forward by fiscal year (KSh million)
pending_rollforward.identity: opening stock + new bills - payments - write-offs or adjustments = closing stock
pending_rollforward.note: Each term is shown only where the year's Controller of Budget report publishes it, with its page. A term the report does not publish is marked "not published"; the closing stock is never worked out from the other terms, and a missing term is never filled. Values are rounded to KSh 0.01 million from the printed figures. Closing stocks for FY 2015/16 to FY 2020/21 are the sum of the published recurrent and development parts.

closing.note: Only development bills were published (KSh 800.34m, PDF p. 249); the county had not worked out a recurrent figure, so no total is published.

health.label: Health in Siaya: Kenya Demographic and Health Surveys 2014 and 2022
health.note: The surveys are the only county-level health series that cover ten years. They are samples, so county values carry a margin of error; small changes should not be over-read. We show no confidence intervals because we have not computed them from the survey tables. Annual routine health data were not retrievable.
